title: Peugeot completes its takeover of Chrysler Europe, which includes the Simca factories in France and the former Rootes Group factories in Britain. The deal was agreed eight months ago. It is unclear whether the Chrysler brand on British…
text: The Rootes Group was a British automobile manufacturer and, separately, a major motor distributors and dealers business. From headquarters in the West End of London, the manufacturer was based in the Midlands and the distribution and dealers business in the south of England.

title: French tanker Betelgeuse explodes at the Gulf Oil terminal at Bantry in Ireland; 50 are killed.
text: Ireland is an island in the North Atlantic Ocean, in Northwestern Europe. Geopolitically, the island is divided between the Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland (part of the United Kingdom – covering the remaining sixth).

title: Peugeot becomes the first carmaker to offer a turbo-diesel engine, fitting the engine to their range-topping 604 saloon. The Simca Horizon is European Car of the Year for 1979.
text: The Peugeot 604 is an executive car produced by the French manufacturer Peugeot from 1975 to 1985. 153,252 cars were sold during its 10-year production life.

title: Cantonales elections held.
text: Cantonale elections to renew canton general councillors were held in France on 18 and 25 March 1979. The left gained 9 presidencies but lost 2.

title: 6 – 8 April – Metz Congress of the French Socialist Party.
text: The Metz Congress was the seventh national congress of the French Socialist Party which took place on 6, 7 and 8 April 1979. The debate was influenced by the failure to update the Common Programme with the French Communist Party (Parti communiste français or PCF), and the unexpected defeat of the "Union of Left" at the 1978 legislative election.

title: Launch of the Peugeot 505, a large rear-wheel drive family saloon which will eventually replace the 504.
text: The Peugeot 505 is a large family car produced by the French manufacturer Peugeot from 1979 to 1992 in Sochaux, France. It was also manufactured in various other countries including Argentina, China, Thailand, Indonesia and Nigeria.

title: A car bomb destroys a Renault owned by "Nazi hunters" Serge and Beate Klarsfeld at their home in France. A note purportedly from ODESSA claims responsibility.
text: Serge Klarsfeld is a Romanian-born French activist and Nazi hunter known for documenting the Holocaust in order to establish the record and to enable the prosecution of war criminals. Since the 1960s, he has made notable efforts to commemorate the Jewish victims of German-occupied France and has been a supporter of Israel.

title: End of the Simca marque after 45 years; from now on, all former Simca and Chrysler cars will be sold as Talbots, following the takeover of Chrysler Europe by Peugeot last year.
text: Talbot is a dormant automobile marque introduced in 1902 by British-French company Clément-Talbot. The founders, Charles Chetwynd-Talbot, 20th Earl of Shrewsbury and Adolphe Clément-Bayard, reduced their financial interests in their Clément-Talbot business during the First World War.

title: French paratroopers help David Dacko to overthrow Bokassa in the Central African Republic.
text: A paratrooper or military parachutist is a soldier trained to conduct military operations by parachuting directly into an area of operations, usually as part of a large airborne forces unit. title: A tsunami in Nice kills 23 people.
text: A tsunamisoo-NAH-mee, (t)suu-; from Japanese: 津波, lit. 'harbour wave', pronounced ) is a series of waves in a water body caused by the displacement of a large volume of water, generally in an ocean or a large lake. Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, underwater explosions, landslides, glacier calvings, meteorite impacts and other disturbances above or below water all have the potential to generate a tsunami.

title: French police shoot dead gangster Jacques Mesrine in Paris.
text: Jacques Mesrine was a French criminal responsible for numerous murders, bank robberies, burglaries, and kidnappings in France, the US, and Canada. Mesrine repeatedly escaped from prison and made international headlines during a final period as a fugitive when his exploits included trying to kidnap the judge who had previously sentenced him.

title: the first running of the Paris–Dakar Rally is won by Alain Génestier, Joseph Terbiaut, and Cyril Neveu
text: 1979 Dakar Rally, also known as the 1979 Paris–Alger–Dakar Rally, was the first running of the Dakar Rally event. The rally began on 26 December 1978 from Paris, France and finished on 14 January 1979 in Dakar, Senegal, interrupted by a transfer across the Mediterranean.

title: Tour de France begins.
text: The 1979 Tour de France was the 66th edition of the Tour de France, one of cycling's Grand Tours. It took place between 27 June and 22 July, with 24 stages covering a distance of 3,765 km.

title: Tour de France ends, won by Bernard Hinault.
text: Bernard Hinault is a French former professional road cyclist. With 147 professional victories, including five times the Tour de France, he is often named among the greatest cyclists of all time.

title: 6 – 9 December – World Judo Championships held in Paris.
text: The 1979 World Judo Championships were the 10th edition of the men's World Judo Championships, and were held in Paris, France from 6–9 December, 1979. The last tournament in 1977 had been cancelled.

title: PSA Peugeot Citroën finalise son rachat de Chrysler Europe, qui comprend les usines Simca en France, le groupe Rootes en Grande-Bretagne et Barreiros en Espagne. Le 10 juillet, les anciennes filiales de Chrysler prennent la marque Talbot.
text: Chrysler Europe était la division européenne du constructeur américain d'automobiles Chrysler Corporation, basée à Vianen, aux Pays-Bas jusqu'en 1978. Il a été formé à partir du rachat et de la fusion des constructeurs français Simca, anglais Rootes et espagnol Barreiros.

title: premier vol du Mirage 4000, un prototype d'avion de chasse de Dassault Aviation.

Il est le dérivé technologique du Mirage 2000 : ils partagent de nombreuses caractéristiques comme leurs moteurs, leurs ailes delta et les commandes de vol électriques.

title: 27 mars : conférence de l’OPEP à Genève. Le prix du pétrole augmente de 10 %. Début du deuxième choc pétrolier. Le prix du baril de pétrole « Arabe léger » passe de 13,34 à 18 dollars de janvier à juillet, jusqu’à 32 dollars en novembre.
text: Le deuxième choc pétrolier est une crise mondiale des prix du pétrole survenue à la fin des années 1970, principalement provoquée par la révolution iranienne de 1979, puis aggravée par la guerre Iran-Irak à partir de 1980. Sous les effets conjugués de la révolution iranienne, de la guerre Iran-Irak et des perturbations de l'offre pétrolière, le prix du pétrole est multiplié par environ 2,5 à 3 entre 1978 et 1981.
